Author: Ravindra Maithani
Bench: Ravindra Maithani
High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 First Bail Application No.1075 of 2024
Amit Kumar ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
Present:-
 Mr. Raj Kumar Singh, Advocate for the applicant.
 Mr. M.A. Khan, Aga for the State.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)

The applicant is in judicial custody in FIR/Case Crime No.91 of 2024, dated 29.03.2024, under
Section 376(3) Ipc and Sections 5(j)(ii)/6 of The Protection Of Children From Sexual Offences Act,
2012, Police Station Kotwali Kotdwar, District Pauri Garhwal.
He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.

According to the FIR, the co-accused, who happens to be the uncle ("Fufa") of the victim established relations with the victim, a young girl of 15 years some 3- 4 months prior to the lodging of the FIR.

4. During the course of investigation, in her statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("the Code"), the victim revealed that, in fact, her boy friend established physical relations with her, who is the applicant.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the FIR is named against the co-accused and this is what the victim has stated in her examination under Section 161 of the Code; in the statement under Section 164 of the Code, the victim did not reveal the name of the applicant as accused.
6. Learned State counsel would submit that the victim in her statement under Section 164 of the Code has stated that the act was done by her boy friend.
He would submit that the charge-sheet is submitted against both, the boy friend and the uncle.

sentences.text: It is the stage of bail.
Much of the discussion at this stage is to be avoided.
To the extent of appreciating the controversy the matter may be examined with the caveat that any observation made at this stage shall have no bearing at any subsequent stage of the case.
8. The FIR is not named against the applicant.
It is specifically against the co-accused.
In her statement under Section 164 of the Code, the applicant named the boy friend, who committed the offence.
She did not name the boy friend.
In her statement under Section 164 of the Code, she did nothing even to mention the name of boy friend, but said that her uncle committed act with her.
The statement of the victim appears to be wavering.
It makes out a case for bail.
9. Having considered, this Court is of the view that it is a case fit for bail and the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
10. The bail application is allowed.
11. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 14.06.2024
